paper_metadata.title: Improvement of deep drawing formability of Mg-6Al-1Zn magnesium alloy sheets with high strength utilizing aging precipitation

evidence.quote: The effects of aging precipitation on microstructure, deep drawing formability and tensile properties, were investigated for Mg-6Al-1Zn (AZ61) alloy sheets.

The average ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and yield strength (YS) are improved by aging treatment from 290 MPa to 306 MPa and from 159 MPa to 177 MPa at RT, respectively, as a result of the formation of Mg 17 Al 12 precipitates in nanoscale.
Mg 17 Al 12 precipitates exert an effect on the restriction of twin growth during deep drawing, which delays the strengthening of deformation texture and in turn suppresses cracking at the edge.
the restrictions of growth of tensile twins and basal slip due to Mg 17 Al 12 precipitates, resulting in the delayed texture strengthening during deformation.

the delayed grain rotation and thus the delayed texture strengthening can be mainly attributed to the restricted growth of tensile twins and the huge hindrance of basal dislocation movement caused by prismatic plate precipitates in the twinned region.
The decreased Al concentration in the α -Mg matrix may cause the increase in stacking fault energy (SFE)
the increase in SFE tends to favor the activity of cross slip [28] . This is beneficial for enhancing dynamic recovery and in turn the improvement of PUE
